restaurants.name: Enish (Oxford Street)
restaurants.curatorNote: Classic Nigerian just off Oxford Street: jollof, egusi with pounded yam, suya.

restaurants.name: Akoko
restaurants.curatorNote: Fine-dining West African tasting menu. Pan-regional rather than purely Nigerian.

restaurants.name: Zeret Kitchen
restaurants.curatorNote: Family-run Ethiopian in Camberwell for big injera platters, with a coffee ceremony. Hours vary, so check.

restaurants.name: Gebeta Ethiopian Kitchen
restaurants.curatorNote: Ethiopian kitchen with coffee ceremony and monthly cultural nights.

restaurants.name: Mosob
restaurants.curatorNote: Long-running Eritrean spot reopened under new management; serves Eritrean and Ethiopian.

restaurants.name: Merhaba Restaurant & Bar
restaurants.curatorNote: Brixton spot serving Eritrean and Ethiopian food together, so not a pure Eritrean pick.

restaurants.name: Sabiib (Harringay)
restaurants.curatorNote: Sabiib's second site (June 2025). Haniid lamb shoulder with sabaayad. Fully halal.

restaurants.name: Sabiib (Acton)
restaurants.curatorNote: Original Sabiib (June 2023). Mogadishu-inspired décor. Haniid and suqaar stars. Halal, alcohol-free.

restaurants.name: High Timber
restaurants.curatorNote: Riverside steakhouse owned by a Stellenbosch wine estate: SA wines, biltong, malva pudding. Food mostly European. Weekdays only.

restaurants.name: Devi Deluxe
restaurants.curatorNote: Family-run Mauritian: dholl puri, bowl renverse, curries. Closed Tuesdays.

restaurants.name: Dhall Puri Factory
restaurants.curatorNote: Mauritian street food in Leyton, formerly Mauritian Delights: dhall puri, biryani, curries. Walk-ins; reportedly cash only.

restaurants.name: Ma Petite Jamaica (Shoreditch)
restaurants.curatorNote: Jamaican diner with a jerk pit, curry goat and rum cocktails, plus live reggae. Second site after Camden.

restaurants.name: Ma Petite Jamaica (Camden)
restaurants.curatorNote: London's first Caribbean diner (2015): jerk wings, rum cocktails and reggae.

restaurants.name: Trini Vibez
restaurants.curatorNote: Trinidadian roti shop: doubles, aloo pie, curry goat. Takeaway. Two addresses reported; phone ahead.

restaurants.name: MAKA Peruvian Cuisine
restaurants.curatorNote: Peruvian: ceviche, lomo saltado, causa and pisco. Closed Mon-Tue.

restaurants.name: Señor Ceviche (Soho)
restaurants.curatorNote: Peruvian and Nikkei (Japanese-Peruvian) small plates with pisco bar at Kingly Court.

restaurants.name: Papelón
restaurants.curatorNote: Venezuelan arepas, cachapas and empanadas on gluten-free corn. Street-food style, with sister sites around London.

restaurants.name: Arepa & Co (Haggerston)
restaurants.curatorNote: Venezuelan arepas and cachapas by Regent's Canal. Famous weekend brunch.

restaurants.name: El Rancho De Lalo
restaurants.curatorNote: Family Colombian started by Lalo (2010). Bandeja paisa, empanadas, patacones. Now Brixton Hill.

restaurants.name: Buen Ayre
restaurants.curatorNote: Tiny Argentine parrilla since 2004. Charcoal-grilled steaks and Argentine wine list.

restaurants.name: La Patagonia
restaurants.curatorNote: Family-run Argentine parrilla since 2010: charcoal-grilled beef, empanadas, sorrentinos. Evenings; weekends from noon.

restaurants.name: Fonda
restaurants.curatorNote: Santiago Lastra's regional Mexican, just off Regent Street. Opened October 2024.

restaurants.name: Mestizo
restaurants.curatorNote: Long-running regional Mexican with tequila and mezcal. Chelsea branch also.

restaurants.name: Ikhaltos Valley
restaurants.curatorNote: Family-run Georgian in Stoke Newington: khinkali, khachapuri, wine. Opened early 2026.

restaurants.name: Qarva (Kensington)
restaurants.curatorNote: Georgian with qvevri amber wines. Kensington branch; sister in Pimlico. Closed Monday lunch.

restaurants.name: Jakobs
restaurants.curatorNote: Long-running Armenian family cafe. The menu mixes Armenian, Persian and Middle Eastern dishes, so a looser fit.

restaurants.name: Land of Fire
restaurants.curatorNote: Cosy Azerbaijani near King's Cross: piti, levengi, plov. Closed Mondays; weekday evenings only. Phone ahead.

restaurants.name: Uzbek Corner (Streatham)
restaurants.address: 2 Central Parade, Streatham High Rd, London
restaurants.curatorNote: Homemade Uzbek plov, manti, samsa and hand-pulled lagman. Moved from Queensway/Bayswater.

restaurants.name: OshPaz (Regent Street)
restaurants.curatorNote: Chef Muzaffar Sadykov's Uzbek: plov, lagman, manti. Vegan options. Grab-and-go by day.

restaurants.name: Marokand
restaurants.curatorNote: Uzbek in Bow: plov, samsa, lagman and manti. HMC halal. Book via WhatsApp.

restaurants.name: Lahpet (Covent Garden)
restaurants.curatorNote: Burmese specialist in The Yards: tea leaf salad, mohinga.

restaurants.name: Lahpet Larder (London Bridge)
restaurants.curatorNote: Burmese restaurant and deli on Bermondsey Street near London Bridge. Closed Sundays.

restaurants.name: Kasa & Kin
restaurants.curatorNote: Filipino all-day diner and bakery from Romulo Cafe team. Family-style plates, ube.

restaurants.name: Donia
restaurants.address: 2.14 Top Floor, Kingly Court, Carnaby St, London
restaurants.curatorNote: Modern Filipino at Kingly Court. Closed Mondays; book ahead.

restaurants.name: Inihaw (Charlton)
restaurants.curatorNote: Filipino grill (inihaw) in Charlton. Dine-in and takeaway. Closed Wednesdays.

restaurants.name: Malay Fellas
restaurants.curatorNote: Modern halal Malaysian in Bayswater. Nasi lemak, beef rendang wagyu and roti.

restaurants.name: Padi@London
restaurants.curatorNote: Halal Singaporean-Malay food (nasi ambeng, rendang, satay), opened April 2026. Not strictly Malaysian, so a curator call.

restaurants.name: Hoppers (Soho)
restaurants.curatorNote: Original Soho location. Sri Lankan hoppers, kothu and roasts. Some South Indian dosas.

restaurants.name: The Coconut Island (Angel)
restaurants.curatorNote: Sri Lankan street food: hoppers, kothu, devilled plates and arrack cocktails.

restaurants.name: Taste of Nepal (Blackfriars Rd)
restaurants.curatorNote: Casual Nepali counter: momos, thukpa, chowmein and curries.

restaurants.name: Lao Café
restaurants.curatorNote: Lao menu from Rosa's Thai team. Char-grilled meats, herbs and curries. Listed as Thai, but Lao.

restaurants.name: Heng Heng at The Red Cow
restaurants.curatorNote: Cambodian and Thai kitchen inside the Red Cow pub, so a curator exception to the specialist rule.

restaurants.name: BAO (Soho)
restaurants.curatorNote: Original BAO (2015). Modern Taiwanese: gua bao and small plates. Walk-ins only.

restaurants.name: Din Tai Fung (Centre Point)
restaurants.address: Unit R04, 11 St Giles Square, London
restaurants.curatorNote: Taiwanese dumpling chain famous for xiao long bao. Book ahead.

restaurants.name: Sông Quê Café
restaurants.curatorNote: Long-running Hoxton institution since 2002. Pho and banh mi on Kingsland Road Pho Mile.

restaurants.name: Bếp House
restaurants.curatorNote: Vietnamese in Hoxton, formerly Ant House. Pho, banh mi, sizzling plates and street food.

restaurants.name: Miód Malina
restaurants.curatorNote: Family-run Polish in Acton: pierogi, żurek, golabki. Closes early.

restaurants.name: Ognisko
restaurants.curatorNote: Polish classics in the Polish Hearth Club townhouse. Central and Eastern European menu, house vodkas.

restaurants.name: TrioBite
restaurants.curatorNote: Hungarian and Romanian menu near Leyton Midland Road: goulash and more. Shared cuisine; Lakehouse is the purer pick.

restaurants.name: Lakehouse Hungarian Restaurant
restaurants.curatorNote: Sibling-run Hungarian in South Woodford. Dine-in first and last weekend of month only.

restaurants.name: Noroc
restaurants.curatorNote: Homely Romanian: sarmale, mamaliga, Moldavian tochitura on Green Lanes.

restaurants.name: La Papy
restaurants.curatorNote: Small Romanian-run in Leyton. Seafood-led menu with Romanian dishes like sarmale.

restaurants.name: Tatar Bunar
restaurants.curatorNote: Ukrainian in Shoreditch with open kitchen. Recipes from Tatarbunary, southern Ukraine. Book SevenRooms.

restaurants.name: Ole Kyiv (Old Street)
restaurants.curatorNote: Independent Ukrainian bar and grill (former Alchemist). Borscht, chicken Kyiv, varenyky. Live music.

restaurants.name: Luso
restaurants.curatorNote: Contemporary Portuguese in Fitzrovia. Closed Sundays; Monday dinner only.

restaurants.name: Casa do Frango (Southwark)
restaurants.curatorNote: Algarve piri-piri chicken on wood charcoal grill, hidden bar. By Borough Market.

restaurants.name: Ekstedt at The Yard
restaurants.address: Great Scotland Yard Hotel, 3-5 Great Scotland Yard, London
restaurants.curatorNote: Niklas Ekstedt's open-fire cooking: Nordic technique, British produce, Swedish chef. Pricey, and not strictly Swedish.

restaurants.name: Marhaba Kabul
restaurants.curatorNote: Afghan charcoal grill: kabuli platter and feast platters. 100% halal. Some Mediterranean starters.

restaurants.name: Afghan Eats
restaurants.curatorNote: Afghan grill on Brick Lane. Chapli kebabs, lamb karahi. Dine-in, takeaway and delivery.

restaurants.name: Diwan Al Yemen
restaurants.curatorNote: Yemeni mandi and haneeth with floor seating on Edgware Road.

restaurants.name: Yemen Land
restaurants.curatorNote: Newer Yemeni: mandi, haneeth, zurbian, malawah. Table or floor seating. Halal.

restaurants.name: Akub
restaurants.curatorNote: Modern Palestinian from chef Fadi Kattan. Opened December 2022.

restaurants.name: Taste of Palestine
restaurants.curatorNote: Takeaway Palestinian. Sister site is mandi-focused, so menu may lean Yemeni.

restaurants.name: Al Sulaymaniyah
restaurants.curatorNote: Iraqi and Kurdish grill: kebabs and big portions. Kurdish-leaning rather than purely Iraqi.

restaurants.name: Samad Al Iraqi
restaurants.curatorNote: Iraqi speciality: masgouf (grilled carp) needs pre-ordering. Also quzi and kubbah.

restaurants.name: Asafo
restaurants.curatorNote: Long-running Ghanaian chop bar: jollof, waakye, banku, fufu with soups. Good food, slow service; a better pick is wanted.

restaurants.name: Fogo de Chão (Soho)
restaurants.curatorNote: Brazilian rodizio steakhouse chain (curator exception).

restaurants.name: Bali Bali
restaurants.curatorNote: Family-owned Indonesian near Covent Garden for 30+ years: rendang, sate, nasi goreng. Menu leans Indonesian-Malaysian.
